name: Sandra Gómez
about:
I'm a multidisciplinary designer based in Barcelona, passionate about the intersection of art, technology, and human experience. I work across AI creative direction, immersive installations, interactive media, and photography — always searching for the emotional core of every project.

Currently pursuing a Master of Science in Digital Arts and Creative Technologies at La Salle Barcelona. Before that, years of hands-on work crafting campaigns, visual identities, and spatial experiences for brands and cultural projects.

I believe great design doesn't just look good — it makes people feel something.

projects.approach:
I combined AI image generation with careful art direction to keep every render on-brand — matching Escribà's real product textures, packaging and studio lighting so the final images could sit next to traditional photography without looking out of place.

Each visual went through multiple generation and retouching passes, refining composition, color and detail until the output reached campaign-ready quality.

Testing happened directly in the space with real visitors, adjusting sensitivity and timing until the experience felt immediate and intuitive.

projects.approach:
We developed the experience as a progressive audiovisual narrative divided into six stages: activation, digital saturation, collapse, bodily awareness, human reconnection, and final decision.

The installation begins inside a familiar cyberpunk environment where visitors are invited to scan a projected QR code. This apparently ordinary interaction gradually destabilizes the space: every scan distorts the city, triggers alerts, and increases the audiovisual tension. The spectators unknowingly participate in creating the system’s collapse.

As the experience progresses, infinite scrolling, advertisements, calls, notifications, artificial voices, and system errors begin to overlap. Visitors’ interactions increase a visible stress level until the environment reaches total overload. The projection glitches, the connection is lost, and the room falls into a complete blackout.

After the collapse, the installation removes screens and digital stimuli. Subtle lighting, breathing, footsteps, and unprocessed organic sounds return attention to the visitors’ bodies and to the physical presence of others. A post-digital natural landscape then appears alongside questions about the relationship between user and device.

The experience ends without offering a definitive solution. Visitors recover their phones as the final message appears:

“Simulacrum 0 has ended. Your choice begins now.”

The audience must decide what to do next.
deliverables: Immersive installation concept and creative direction
Motion graphics and glitch visual language
Reflection on notifications, social media, and connectivity
projects.title: Mini Interactive Experience
projects.content:
SIMULACRUM 0 is an interactive immersive installation that explores our dependence on smartphones, social media, notifications, and constant digital connectivity. The project was partly inspired by the widespread blackout in Spain and the collective sense of disorientation that emerged when communication networks, internet access, and everyday digital services suddenly became unavailable.

The experience asks what happens when the systems we rely on disappear—and whether constant connection has made us more capable or increasingly dependent. Through projection, spatial sound, lighting, mobile interaction, and moments of complete darkness, the installation takes visitors from digital comfort and overstimulation to technological collapse, physical awareness, and human reconnection.

Rather than presenting technology as entirely negative, the project questions the amount of control we have over our devices and how much control they exercise over our behavior.
projects.description: A self-contained interactive experience — not a game, but an immersive journey through sound, visuals and touch.

projects.approach:
I followed the tour as it naturally unfolded, documenting the interaction between the visitors, the artworks and the studio itself. Rather than staging every moment, we focused on authentic reactions, movement and spontaneous details.

The photography explored the different areas of Studio 46—from its gallery rooms and original architectural features to its printing presses, tools and working spaces. The visual direction combined wider environmental shots with close-up details to communicate the studio’s intimate, lived-in character and its connection to generations of artists.
deliverables: Visual documentation of the studio’s creative process
projects.title: Studio 46
projects.content:
Studio 46 approached me to create a series of photographs that could capture the character of the space while visitors experienced a guided tour. Located in a historic family home in Barcelona’s Gràcia neighbourhood, the studio brings together architecture, printmaking, contemporary art and decades of artistic heritage.

The images were created for the studio’s website and digital communication, with the aim of presenting not only the artworks, but also the atmosphere, history and unique details visitors encounter throughout the space.
